title: Retirement money vs. short goal
description: Retirement account early-withdrawal risk vs. short time horizon
condition: time_horizon_years <= max_horizon_years AND value in ['401k', 'IRA'] accounts > 0
flag: Retirement funds (401k/IRA) held against a short-term goal — early withdrawal penalties may apply before funds are needed
why: Money in a 401k or IRA usually can't be withdrawn before age 59½ without a 10% penalty plus income tax, so it shouldn't be counted on for a goal only a few years away.

title: Single-position concentration
condition: max single position value (excluding cash equivalents and broadly diversified index funds) / total portfolio value > max_position_pct
why: Holding too much in one company or narrow theme ties the client's outcome to a single bet. Cash and broadly diversified index funds (e.g. total-market or aggregate bond funds) are exempt because they already spread risk across hundreds of issuers.

title: Volatility vs. conservative profile
description: High-volatility exposure vs. conservative risk tolerance
flag: Conservative client holds {pct}% in high-volatility holdings ({tickers})
why: A client who said they want to avoid big swings shouldn't hold much in securities that routinely move 40%+ in a year.

title: Liquidity need vs. accessible money
description: Liquidity need vs. accessible account balance
condition: liquidity_need == 'high' AND (savings + checking + brokerage_taxable value) / total portfolio value < min_accessible_pct
flag: High liquidity need but only {pct}% held in readily accessible accounts (savings, checking, taxable brokerage)
why: A client who may need cash soon must be able to reach it without penalties, so at least a quarter should sit in savings, checking or a taxable brokerage account.

title: Debt-adjusted risk
flag: Client carries significant existing debt (${existing_other_debt}) while holding {pct}% in high-volatility assets — compounding financial risk
why: Carrying significant non-mortgage debt while holding volatile assets compounds risk: a market drop can coincide with debt payments coming due.

title: Age-based equity ceiling
flag: Equity allocation ({pct}%) significantly exceeds the typical benchmark for client's age bracket ({benchmark}%)
why: Clients nearing retirement have less time to recover from a downturn, so equity exposure far above the age benchmark is flagged.
